segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏣᎳᎩ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: tsalagi aniwonisgv dohv?
segments.translation: They were Cherokee speakers, right?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: RᏧᎳ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎡᏙᏓᎮᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᏲᏁᎦ ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏱᎦᏬᏂᎮ ᎨᎮ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏍᏔᎾ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏭᏟ ᎢᎦ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎦᏬᏂᎮ ᎡᏥᏃ ᎤᎪᏓ ᏌᏚᏏᏁᏛ ᎨᎵ ᏫᏚᏍᏆᏛ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎤᏑᎵᎪᏨ, ᏧᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ ᎤᎪᏓ ᏲᏁᎦ, ᎦᏬᏂᎲ
segments.transliteration: Rtsula tsalagi edodahena, tsigehv tla howa yonega gawonisgv yigehe yigawonihe gehe sgi yinulisstana aseno wutli iga tsalagi gawonihe etsino ugoda sadusinedv geli widusquadv sginana nahiyu usuligotsv, tsudeloquasdi ugoda yonega, gawonihv
segments.translation: They both spoke Cherokee. My dad didn’t speak English, he would talk it if he had to, but he mostly talked Cherokee. Mom, more so. She graduated the eleventh grade. When she quit school, that’s when she talked more English.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏩᏩᎨᏩ ᏍᎩᏃ ᏝᏍ ᏝᏍ ᏨᏥ Ꮎ ᏧᎾᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ ᏥᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁ ᏱᎨᎮ?
segments.transliteration: wawagewa sgino tlas tlas tsvtsi na tsunadeloquasdi tsidulvwisdane yigehe?
segments.translation: I forgot now. Didn’t your mom work at school, too?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᎥᎥ. ᎤᎾ ᎪᎢ ᏧᎴᏅᎲ ᏢᏛᎮ High School ᏩᏩᎴᏅ ᎾᎯᏳᏢ ᎤᎴᏅᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏕᎨᏲᎲᏍᎬ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏣᎳᎩ. ᎤᎾᎮᎾ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏠᏱ ᎾᏩᎵᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗ ᎯᎾᎾ ᎢᎦᏓ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ Ꮭ ᏯᏃᎵᎨ ᏲᏁᎦ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏕᎦᏁᏢᏓᏁᎲ ᏓᏍᏕᎵᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎢᎪᎯᏗᏛ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ ᏂᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎥᎾᎾ ‘Teacher’s aide’ ᏓᏃᎮ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎢᎸᏍᎩᎮᎾᏴ ᎯᏍᎩ ᎨᎵ ᏯᏂ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎾᎾᏛᏁᎲᏅ ᎪᎢ ᏗᎾᏕᏲᎲᏍᎩ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏓᏂᏍᏕᎵᎲ. ᏲᏎᎡ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎠᏯ ᏗᎦᏕᎶᏆᏍᎬ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏳᏂᎧᎮ ᎡᎵᏛᎮ ᎦᎾᎦᏘ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎠᏴ ᎪᎯᏥᎩ.
segments.transliteration: vv. una goi tsulenvhv tlvdvhe High School wawalenv nahiyutlv ulenvhv sgina degeyohvsgv diniyotli tsalagi. unahena squu utloyi nawalisdanelv nigalisdi hinana igada diniyotli tla yanolige yonega sgina deganetlvdanehv dasdelihv sgina igohididv tla yawanata yigohida nidulvwisdanelv vnana ‘Teacher’s aide’ danohe sginana ilvsgihenayv hisgi geli yani sginana nanadvnehvnv goi dinadeyohvsgi diniyotli danisdelihv. yosee nahiyu aya digadeloquasgv sgi yusdi yunikahe elidvhe ganagati yigehe ayv gohitsigi.
segments.translation: Yeah, Greasy high school. When I started high school, that’s about when she started teaching the children Cherokee. Also, what happened to me, happened to the kids. They weren’t speaking English either. She was teaching them how to say the words in English. I don’t know how long she worked there, helping the children. She was a teacher’s aide. There were a few working there doing the same, helping the children. It would’ve been good if they were doing that when I was in school, I probably would’ve been a doctor today.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏣᏙᏓ Ꮩ ᎠᏛᏁ ᏥᎨᎮ?
segments.transliteration: tsadoda do advne tsigehe?
segments.translation: What did your dad do?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: Ꮎ... bridge Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏴᏓ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎬᏗ?
segments.transliteration: na... bridge do usdi yvda tsalagi gvdi?
segments.translation: Bridge… how do you say it in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏂᏒᏢᏗᏍᎬ
segments.transliteration: anisvtlvdisgv
segments.translation: They were building a bridge.

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᎠᏂᏒᏢᏗᏍᎬ ᎥᎾ ᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ. ᏦᎢᏁᎡ ᏗᎧᏂᏙ ᏫᏄᎵᏍᏔᏅ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎥᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᎴᏅᎲ Ꮭ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎩ ᏧᎾᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ ᏃᏊᎴ Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᎠᏕᎳ ᏳᏂᎮ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎠᎾᏝᏅᏢ ᏗᎬᎩᏚᏥ Ꮎ ...ties...railroad ties...Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏴᏓ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎬᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ?
segments.transliteration: anisvtlvdisgv vna dulvwisdanehv. tsoinee dikanido winulistanv sginana vsgina ulenvhv tla osda yigi tsunadeloquasdi noquule tla howa adela yunihe sgina anitsutsa nigada anatlanvtlv digvgidutsi na ...ties...railroad ties...do usdi yvda tsalagi gvdi sgina?
segments.translation: He worked at building bridges. He finished third grade. That’s when he started saying that school was no good, also they hardly had any money. All the boys, my uncles, ties… railroad ties… How do you say it in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏗᏗᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: didisdi
segments.translation: Railroad ties.

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᏗᏗᏍᏗ ᎥᎥ ᎤᎾ,ᎴᏅᎲ ᏓᏃᏢᏍᎬ ᏓᏂᏂ,ᏕᎬ ᎤᎾᏃ ᎡᎵᏛᎮ ᏦᎦᏚᏢ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎨᎮ ᎤᏩᏌ ᎾᏛᏁᎮᏃ ᏕᎦᏂᏕᎬ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ. ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᏧᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᏱᎩ ...cause... ᏝᏛ ᏯᎦᏔᎮ ᎤᎪᎵᏰᏗ ᏣᎳᎩᏭ ᎤᏩᏌ ᎠᎦᏔᎲ ᏕᎪᎵᏰᏍᎬ.
segments.transliteration: didisdi vv una,lenvhv danotlvsgv danini,degv unano elidvhe tsogadutlv yudetiyvda gehe uwasa nadvneheno deganidegv sginana. sgina tla howa tsudeloquav yigi ...cause... tladv yagatahe ugoliyedi tsalagiwu uwasa agatahv degoliyesgv.
segments.translation: They started making railroad ties and selling them. Probably, he was about 13 years old, he was doing it by himself and selling them. Since he hardly went to school, he didn’t know how to read. He only knew how to read Cherokee.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎥᎾᏭᏍᏊ ᏗᏣᏕᏅ ᏍᏊ ᎤᎾᏕᏅ ᎨᎲ ᏕᎨᏣᎦᏴᎵᎨ?
segments.transliteration: vnawusquu ditsadenv squu unadenv gehv degetsagayvlige?
segments.translation: Were they born the same place where you were born?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᎥᎥ. ᎤᎾᎡ ᎡᏙᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎪᎢᎮᎾ ᎤᎾ Mom ᎨᎲ Bunch-i ᎤᎾ yeah...Ꮭ ᏭᏟᏴ ᏱᎩ.
segments.transliteration: vv. unae edoda gehv goihena una Mom gehv Bunch-i una yeah...tla wutliyv yigi.
segments.translation: My dad was born in Greasy and my mom at Bunch, yeah… not far.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏗᎨᏣᎦᏴᎵᎨ...ᏗᎨᏣᎵᏏᏃᎲ ᏗᎨᏣᎵᏏ Ꮩ ᏚᎾᏙᎡ?
segments.transliteration: digetsagayvlige...digetsalisinohv digetsalisi do dunadoe?
segments.translation: Your parents… your grandparents, what were their names?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᎡᏚᏛ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏙᏓ ᎡᏚᏛ ᏗᎦᏃᏣᏟ ᏚᏙᎥ ᎾᎾ ᎤᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏑᏌᏂ ᏚᏙᎥ Ꮎ ᎡᏥ ᎡᎵᏏ ᎾᏂ ᏧᏟ ᏚᏙᎥ ᎾᏂ ᎠᏃᏎᎲ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔᏃ ᎤᏙᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎾᎮᎾ Charlie Twist ᏚᏙᎥ ᏩᏩᏕᎳᎰᏒᏃ ᎣᏂ ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏥᎪᎡ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎦᏳᎳ ᏁᎲᎾ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᏴ ᎠᏩᏕᏅ.
segments.transliteration: edudv edoda tsigehv udoda edudv diganotsatli dudov nana usdayvhvsgi elisi susani dudov na etsi elisi nani tsutli dudov nani anosehv tla yawanatano udoda gehv nahena Charlie Twist dudov wawadelahosvno oni sgina tla ilvhiyu tsigoe sginana gayula nehvna gehv na ayv awadenv.
segments.translation: My dad’s dad —Diganotsatli was his name. And his wife, Granny, Susan was her name. My mom’s mom, Grandma, Nan Tsutli, was her name, they called her Nan. I don’t know about her dad. Her dad’s name was Charlie Twist, they found out later, but I never got to see him. He had already passed, when I was born.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏩᎾᏔ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎤᏓᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏨᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ.
segments.transliteration: awanata osda udasdayvdi gehv tsvtsi tsigehv.
segments.translation: I know your mom was a good cook.

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: Yeah.
segments.transliteration: Yeah.
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏂᎯ ᎭᏓᏅᏖᏍᎬ Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏫᏓᏤᏢ ᎨᎲ ᏣᎸᏉᏕ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬ ᏣᎩᏍᏗ?
segments.transliteration: nihi hadanvtesgv do usdi widatsetlv gehv tsalvquode adasdayvhvsgv tsagisdi?
segments.translation: Thinking back, what did you like the best of what she cooked?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᏚᏯ, ᏄᎾ, ᎾᏅ...ᏭᏟᏴ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᎦᏚ ᏧᏬᏢᏗ. Boy...ᎠᏯ ᎭᎴ ᎠᏟᎢᏢ ᎠᎩᎪᎥ ᏱᎩ ᏍᎩᏴ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏓᏃᏢᏍᎬ ᏏᏅ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎾᎥᎢ ᎾᎾᏛᏁᎭ ᎠᎩᏙ ᎠᎦᏍᎦᏂᏗ ᏥᏲᏎᎰ. ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎾᎥ ᏧᏬᏢᏗ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ.
segments.transliteration: duya, nuna, nanv...wutliyv gehv na gadu tsuwotlvdi. Boy...aya hale atliitlv agigov yigi sgiyv osda danotlvsgv sinv etsi tsigehv. navi nanadvneha agido agasganidi tsiyoseho. sginana nav tsuwotlvdi sginana.
segments.translation: Beans, potatoes, but mostly the bread she made. Boy, I have never seen somebody make bread like Mom did. My sister comes close. I call her Lefty. She comes close to making bread like Mom.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Ꭼ.Ꮒ ᎨᏒ ᎢᎩᏅᏁᎸ ᎠᎩᏍᎦᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᎧᏃᎮ.
segments.transliteration: gv.ni gesv iginvnelv agisgayvhvsgi kanohe.
segments.translation: Let’s make it known—he’s talking about my wife.

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎦ) ᎥᎥ. ᎨᏳᏁᎩ ᎠᏮᎨᏩ ᏣᎳᎩ Ꭹ.Ꮃ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ. ᎨᏳᏁᎩ, ᎠᎩᏙ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎾᎥᎢ ᏱᏕᎪᏢᎾ.
segments.transliteration: (uyetsi,sga) vv. geyunegi awvgewa tsalagi gi.la yigohida. geyunegi, agido sgina navi yidegotlvna.
segments.translation: Geyunegi, I forgot Cherokee right away. Geyunegi is my sister. She can make it pretty close like Mom.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Umm...ᎯᏅᏗᏍᎪᏍ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴᏗ?
segments.transliteration: Umm...hinvdisgos sgiyusdi adasdayvdi?
segments.translation: Do you miss this kind of cooking?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᏂᎪᎸ...ᏂᎪᎸ. Ꮭ ᏕᎦ ᎠᏩᏚᎵᏍᎪ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏓᏍᏓᏴᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏥᎦᏗ ᏳᏓᎭ ᏫᏥᏫ,Ꮫ.Ꭿ--ᎢᏥᏫ,--TᏨᏫ,Ꮫ.ᎯᏙᎰ ᏍᏊ ᎠᎩᏲᎰ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏩᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ.
segments.transliteration: nigolv...nigolv. tla dega awadulisgo etsi tsigehv udasdayvnv sgina, tsigadi yudaha witsiwi,dv.hi--itsiwi,--Ttsvwi,dv.hidoho squu agiyoho sgiyusdi awalisdayvdi.
segments.translation: All the time. I really want my mom’s cooking. That’s why I come visit you all, just looking for this kind of food to eat.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏯ ᎦᏓᏅᏖᏍᎪ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏫᎨᏙᎲ ᏣᏩᎴᏅᎲ.
segments.transliteration: aya gadanvtesgo agvyi wigedohv tsawalenvhv.
segments.translation: I sometimes think when I first went to visit you all.

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: Uh huh.
segments.transliteration: Uh huh.
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Pork chops ᏚᏒᏂ,Ꮫ.ᏍᎬ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: Pork chops dusvni,dv.sgv gehv
segments.translation: She cooked pork chops.

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: Uh huh.
segments.transliteration: Uh huh.
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏱᎦ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎠᏩᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᎨᎵᏍᎬ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: yiga osda awalisdayvdi gelisgv gehv
segments.translation: I thought it was good to eat.

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: Yeah, ᎢᎦᏓ,Ꮫ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎾᎮᎾ ᎨᏳᏁᎩ ᎾᏅ ᎾᏂ ᏚᏙᎥ ᏍᏊ ᎠᎩᏙ Ꮠ ᎨᎨᏲᏅ Ꭴ--... Ꮎ ‘Milk,’ ᏕᎦᎵᏙᏗ Ꮎ ‘Milk Crates’ ᏓᏃᎮᎰ ᎥᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᎩ.Ꮈ ᎠᎩᏙ Ꮣ--ᏕᎬᏗᏰᏍᎬ ᏃᏊᎴᏅ Ꮠ ᏑᏌ--ᎾᏂ ᎤᏍᏗᎬ.ᎮᎾ ᏍᎩᎾ. ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮎ milk crateᎢ ᎤᎩ.Ꮈ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏕᎬ--Ꮎ-- ᏓᎧᏲᏗᎲ. ᎤᏓᏍᏓᏴᏗᏃ ᎡᎵᏛᎮ ᏔᎵᏢ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎨᎮ ᎨᏳᏁᎩ ᎤᎾ ᎤᏓᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᎾᎬᏁᎴ ᎡᏙᏓ ᎠᏥᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬ ᏒᎾᎴ ᎡᎯ ᏧᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎴ--ᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎴᏒ.
segments.transliteration: Yeah, igada,dv osda gehv adasdayvdi aseno nahena geyunegi nanv nani dudov squu agido so gegeyonv u--... na ‘Milk,’ degalidodi na ‘Milk Crates’ danoheho vsgina ugi.lv agido da--degvdiyesgv noquulenv so susa--nani usdigv.hena sgina. sgina na milk cratei ugi.lv squu sgina degv--na-- dakayodihv. udasdayvdino elidvhe talitlv yudetiyvda gehe geyunegi una udasdayvdi nagvnele edoda atsisdayvhvsgv svnale ehi tsulvwisdanele--dulvwisdanelesv.
segments.translation: Yeah, she was a good cook, Geyunegi. And Nan, my other sister. Mom taught them to cook. Those milk crates, that’s what they used to stand on to wash dishes. The other sister, Nan, she was smaller/younger, she also stood on a crate to dry dishes. Geyunegi, she was about two when they made her cook breakfast for dad before he went to work.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᏍᎩ-ᏍᎩᏃᎯᏏ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏣᏛᏒ Ꮎ um...ᏕᎭᏟᎶᏍᏓᏭ ᎢᎾᎨ ᏱᎩ, ᎠᎹᏱ, ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏄᏍᏛ Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏕ Ꮎ ᏣᏛᏒ ᎥᎾ?
segments.transliteration: nana sgi-sginohisi nusdv tsadvsv na um...dehatlilosdawu inage yigi, amayi, sgi yusdi nusdv do usde na tsadvsv vna?
segments.translation: Tell me how you remember what it was like when you grew up. The woods, the river how was it like, where you grew up?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᎢᎾᎨᏛ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎪᎯᏥᏊ ᏳᏟᎶᏓ ᎤᎲ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎮᎾ Ꮎ ᎾᏂ ᏧᏟ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᎦᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏥ ᎡᏂ ᏚᏙᎥ ᎤᏍᏆᏘ ᏚᏙᎥ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏂᏁᎳ ᏍᎩᏅ Ꮩ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᎾ,ᏤᎵ ᎨᎮ. ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎨᏥᏙᎵᏨ ᎡᏥ ᎡᏙᏗ ᏂᎬ. Ꮎ ᏓᏂ,Ꮩ.ᎵᏙᎲ Ꮎ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ Ꮭ Ꮟ ᏱᏚᎾᏓᏘᎾᎥ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎨᏥ--ᎨᏥᏙᎵᏨ ᎯᏛ. ᏱᎬᏂ,ᏗᏅᏏ ᎠᎪᎮᎴ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ. Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏚᎵ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᎢᎸᏢ ᏍᎩ Ꮥ--...Ꮎ...ᎢᎲᏏᏙᎲ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎠᎪᎮᎴ ᎥᏍᎩᎾ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏣᏩᏕᏅ ᎤᎾᎮᎾ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏍᏆᏘ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᎡᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᎠᏂᏁᎵ,Ꮫ BunchᎢ ᎾᎥ ᎤᎾᎮᎾ ᎠᏩᏕᏅ ᎠᏯ. ᎾᎯᏳ ᎠᏩᎳᏂ,ᏥᏢ, ᏍᎩᏅ ᎢᎾᎨ ᎨᎲ ᎾᎾ ᎣᏥᏁᎸ. ᏩᎩ.Ꮕ ᏙᏥᎾᏝᎥ ᏐᏈᎵ ᏃᏊᎴ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ -- ᎣᏍᏓᏛᎮ ᏌᏚᎢᏢ ᏍᎪᎯ ᎴᏱᎦ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᏄᎵᏍᏔᏅ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏥᏃᎭᎵᏙᎲ ᏗᎬᎩᏚᏥ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎡᏙᏓ ᎠᎾᏝᏅᏢ ᎠᏂᏃᎭᎵᏙ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᏅ ᏍᎩ ᎤᏟᎦ ᎨᎲ ᎬᏪᏲᏅ ᎠᎩᏃᎭᎵᏓᏍᏗᎠᏫ ᏚᏂᏲᎲ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎠᏯᎩ ᏌᎶᎵ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏕᏥᏲᎲ ᎠᏮᏌ ᏱᎩ ᏃᏭ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏫ ᏧᏂᏍᏔᏄᏍᏔᏅ ᎥᎾ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎬᏪᏲᎲᏍᎬ ᎦᏥᏍᏓᏩᏕᎬ. ᎡᎵᏛᎮ ᏔᎵ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓᏢ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎦᏥᏍᏓᏩᏕᎬ ᎥᎾᏃ ᎠᏮᏌᏃ ᎠᏩᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏫ ᏗᏱᏍᏗ. ᏃᏊᎴ Mom ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᎸᏉᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎤᏑᏂᏓᏍᏗ ᎥᏍᎩᎾ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎥᏥᏍᏓᏩᏕᎬ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎠᏑᏂᏙᎰ. ᏃᏭᏅ ᎯᎢ-- ᎾᎾ Radient Line ᏍᎩᏭ ᏙᏨ,ᏗᎲ. ᎠᏂᎪᎳ ᏙᏍᏗᏂᏱᏍᎬ ᎥᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏂᏖᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏂᎪᎳ.
segments.transliteration: inagedv gehv sgohitsiquu yutliloda uhv edoda tsigehv sgihena na nani tsutli elisi tsigadi sgina utsi eni dudov usquati dudov sgina aninela sginv do gehv sgina una,tseli gehe. sgina, getsidolitsv etsi edodi nigv. na dani,do.lidohv na galitsode tla si yidunadatinav nahiyu sgina getsi--getsidolitsv hidv. yigvni,dinvsi agohele edoda tsigehv. tla yawaduli diniyotli ilvtlv sgi de--...na...ihvsidohv gusdi agohele vsgina nahiyu tsawadenv unahena sgina usquati tsigehv na eni tsigehv galitsode anineli,dv Bunchi nav unahena awadenv aya. nahiyu awalani,tsitlv, sginv inage gehv nana otsinelv. wagi.nv dotsinatlav soquili noquule ilvhiyu -- osdadvhe saduitlv sgohi leyiga yawadetiyvda nulistanv nigohilv tsinohalidohv digvgidutsi nigada edoda anatlanvtlv aninohalido gehv sginv sgi utliga gehv gvweyonv aginohalidasdiawi duniyohv nigohilv ayagi saloli nigohilv detsiyohv awvsa yigi nowu sgina awi tsunistanustanv vna sgina gvweyohvsgv gatsisdawadegv. elidvhe tali tsudetiyvdatlv sgina gatsisdawadegv vnano awvsano awadeloquav sgina awi diyisdi. noquule Mom tsigehv ulvquodi gehv usunidasdi vsgina noquule sgina vtsisdawadegv osda asunidoho. nowunv hii-- nana Radient Line sgiwu dotsv,dihv. anigola dosdiniyisgv vsgina unitedi gehv squu unigola.
segments.translation: The woods, my dad had 100 acres. My grandma, Nan, Tsutli, her mom was Ann. Usgwati was her husband, it was really theirs. So, they felt sorry for Mom and Dad 'cause they were just renting everywhere, but they didn’t have children then. They felt sorry for him, Usgwati, so they told him they would sell to my dad. “I don’t want the children to be moving all the time ” said Usgwati. When I was born it was Usgwati and Ann, they were living in a house near Bunch, that was where I was born. When I was born, it was wooded where we lived. We had cows and horses and, when I was about ten or eleven, I was always out hunting. All my uncles, my dad’s brothers, were all hunters. They were the ones that taught me to hunt . They were hunting deer all the time. But me, I was always shooting squirrels, when I was by myself. When it was deer season, I followed them, and they taught me. ‘Probably about two years, I followed them. And then I learned how to kill deer by myself. And my mom she loved to go fishing. Then I would go with her to go fishing. We were using Radient Line and caught perches. They were delicious to eat, the perches.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎥᎾ ᎾᎥᏭ ᎤᏪᏴ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: vna navwu uweyv dohv?
segments.translation: The creek/river is close by, right?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᎥᎥ. ᏌᎷᏂᎨᏴ ᎤᏪᏴ ᎠᏃᏎᎰ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᎥᎾᎾ ᏬᏤᏙᎰ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎣᏣᏑᏂᏙᎰ
segments.transliteration: vv. salunigeyv uweyv anoseho. sgina vnana wotsedoho nigohilv otsasunidoho
segments.translation: Yeah, they call it Sallisaw Creek. That’s where we went to fish all the time.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏏᏍ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ, ᎿᏛᏁᎸᎲᏍᎪ ᎪᎯᏥᎩ?
segments.transliteration: sis sgiyusdi, hnadvnelvhvsgo gohitsigi?
segments.translation: Do you still do this today?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᎠᏴᎩ?
segments.transliteration: ayvgi?
segments.translation: Me?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎥᎥ
segments.transliteration: vv
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᏳᏓᎭᏛ ᎥᎥ. Ꮎ ᎠᎩᎸᏉᏗᎮᎾ Ꮎ ᎠᎹᏱ ᎠᏩᏚᏱᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏕᏥᏂᏱᏍᎪ ᎤᏂᎪᎳ ᎤᎾ ᎤᏪᏴ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎪᎯᏗ ᏍᎩ ᎬᏩᏛᏁᎸ.
segments.transliteration: yudahadv vv. na agilvquodihena na amayi awaduyidi sgina detsiniyisgo unigola una uweyv aseno gohidi sgi gvwadvnelv.
segments.translation: Sometimes. I like to be in the water. I catch perches there in the creek, but it’s been a long time since I’ve done it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏝᏍᏊ Oklahoma Ᏹ.ᏅᎪᎪ ᏄᏓᎴᏍᏛ Ꮻ.ᏃᎭᎵᏙᎰ.
segments.transliteration: tlasquu Oklahoma yi.nvgogo nudalesdv wi.nohalidoho.
segments.translation: Do you not go out of Oklahoma to go hunting?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎯᎡ ᎠᏩᏛ.ᏐᏅ ᏗᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓ--ᏗᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁ ᏄᎵᏍᏔᏅ ‘yeah.’ Nebraska ᏬᏤᏙᎲ, Colorado ᏫᎨᏙᎰ ᏃᏭ ᎣᎩᎾᎵ ᎠᏧᏣ ᎣᎩᎾ,ᎵᎪᏐ.
segments.transliteration: vv hie awadv.sonv digilvwi,sda--digilvwi,sdane nulistanv ‘yeah.’ Nebraska wotsedohv, Colorado wigedoho nowu oginali atsutsa ogina,ligoso.
segments.translation: After I grew up and started working, yeah. We’d go to Nebraska, and then I go to Colorado now. My good friend goes with me.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎦᎩ--ᎦᎪ ᏳᎾ,ᏍᏗ, ᎾᎥ ᏂᏣᏛᏅ ᎾᎥ ᎠᏂᏁᎴ?
segments.transliteration: gagi--gago yuna,sdi, nav nitsadvnv nav aninele?
segments.translation: Who was living by you all?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᏚᏙᎥᎾᏛ ᎠᏂᏁᎸ ᏞᎦ, Ꮎ Dad, well my cousin, Jake ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏚᏥ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏪᏥ, ᎨᎲ ᏚᏙᎥᎾ ᎤᎾ Ꭸ.ᏓᎵ ᎠᏂᏁᎸ ᎾᎾ Houston Pettit ᏚᏓᏘᎾᎥ Ꮟ ᎠᏂᏁᎳ ᎡᎵᏛᎲ ᏔᎵ, ᏳᏟᎶᏓ, ᎤᏟᎶᏓ, ᎴᏱᎦ,Ꮲ ᏄᏴᏢ ᏗᏢ ᎠᏂᏁᎳ. ᎤᎾ Arthur Williams ᎤᎾ ᎠᏮ,Ᏼ ᏃᏊᎴ ᎤᎦᎾᏩ ᏗᏢ ᎠᏂᏁᎳ ᎥᎾᎾ ᎠᏂᏔᎵ, ᎠᏂᎨᎱ.Ꮳ, ᏚᏛ.ᎯᏍᏔᏅ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎾ.
segments.transliteration: dudovnadv aninelv tlega, na Dad, well my cousin, Jake tsigehv edutsi, sgina uwetsi, gehv dudovna una ge.dali aninelv nana Houston Pettit dudatinav si aninela elidvhv tali, yutliloda, utliloda, leyiga,tlv nuyvtlv ditlv aninela. una Arthur Williams una awv,yv noquule uganawa ditlv aninela vnana anitali, anigehu.tsa, dudv.histanv squu sgina.
segments.translation: No Name was living by us for a little while. Dad, well my cousin Jake was Dudovn’s uncle and they lived below us. Houston Pettit’s family still live there. They live probably about two miles north of us and Arthur Williams was living just south of us, with two girls that he raised.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏂᎦᏓᏍ ᏏᏓᏁᎸ ᎢᏣᏙᏢ ᏍᎩᎾ?
segments.transliteration: nigadas sidanelv itsadotlv sgina?
segments.translation: Are they all your family, too?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᎫᏍᏗ ᏙᏣᏓᏛᏂ,Ꮧ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎥᎥ ‘yep.’
segments.transliteration: gusdi dotsadadvni,di nigada vv ‘yep.’
segments.translation: We’re all cousins.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏕ ᎠᎾ ᏥᏣᏛ.ᏏᏗᏎ?
segments.transliteration: do usde ana tsitsadv.sidise?
segments.translation: What was it like there, as you were growing up?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᎭᏗ ᎡᎶᎯ ᏥᏂ,ᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅᏍᎬ ᎫᏍᏗ, ᎮᏍᏗ, Ᏺ-ᏲᎦᎾᏖ ᏍᎩᎮᎾᏛ ᏥᎦᏗ ᎢᎾᎨ ᎡᎯ ᎨᎲ Ꮭ-Ꮭ ᏍᎩᏭᏅ ᎢᎦ ᎣᎦᎾᏛ. ᏳᏓᎭᎮᎾ, ᎬᎩ.Ꮻ,Ꮫ.ᎯᏙᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᏂ-Pettit ᏃᏊᎴᏅ ᏍᏊ Sue Ann ᏤᏂᏅ ᏗᎦᎵ,ᏍᎩ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᏪᏥ, ᎠᏂᎨᎱ.Ꮳ, ᎾᎾ ᏙᏥᏩᏛ.ᎯᏙᎲ ᎨᎲ ᏭᏟᏴ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᏁᏙᎲ. ᎥᏍᎩᎾ Ꮭ--ᏍᎩᏭᏅ...that was...Ꮎ ᏙᎩ.ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏴᏓ,? ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᎤᏬᎵ,Ꮧ ᎣᏥᏃᎮᏢᏍᎪ ᎨᎲ. ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮭ--ᏞᏍᏗ, ᎢᎸᏢ ᏲᏤᏙᎮ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏲᎦᎵᏍᏉᎵᏓᏁᎸ Ꮭ ᎤᏣᏘᏅ ᎣᎨᏅᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᏭ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏙᏣᏓᎪᏩ,ᏘᎲ.
segments.transliteration: hadi elohi tsini,gali,stanvsgv gusdi, hesdi, yo-yoganate sgihenadv tsigadi inage ehi gehv tla-tla sgiwunv iga oganadv. yudahahena, gvgi.wi,dv.hidohv na ani-Pettit noquulenv squu Sue Ann tseninv digali,sgi, tsigehv tsuwetsi, anigehu.tsa, nana dotsiwadv.hidohv gehv wutliyv gehv adanelv anedohv. vsgina tla--sgiwunv...that was...na dogi.yusdi, yvda,? gohusdi, uwoli,di otsinohetlvsgo gehv. sgina tla--tlesdi, ilvtlv yotsedohe tla ilvhiyu yogalisquolidanelv tla utsatinv ogenvsdi sgiwu nigada dotsadagowa,tihv.
segments.translation: We didn’t know anything. Like what is going in the world today—that’s what I mean. We just lived in the woods, that’s all we knew. Sometimes the Pettits would visit me. Also Sue, Ann, and Jan (Arthur Williams’ girls) we would all visit each other. But mostly they were at our house. We would tell funny stories because we didn’t go anywhere. They wouldn’t let us go anywhere. So that’s all we had to do, just visit.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Ꮎ ᏍᏆᏞᏍᏗ ᏣᎾᏁᏦᏂᏙᎲ Ꮳ,ᏠᏯᏍᏔᏂᏙᎸᏍ?
segments.transliteration: na squatlesdi tsananetsonidohv tsa,tloyastanidolvs?
segments.translation: When they had ball games around, did you get to play?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎥᎥ ᎡᎵᏛ ᎦᎵ,ᏉᎩ’Ꮲ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᎠᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᏕᎦᏁᎶᎲᏍᎬ. ᏍᎩ ᏩᏩᏛ.ᏐᏅ ᎢᎦ Ꮥ ᏔᎵᏍᎪᎯ’Ꮲ ᎾᏩᏕᏘᏴ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏣᎩ,ᏑᎵ,ᎪᏨ ᎣᏂ. ᎠᎩᏄᎸᏅ ᎠᏓᎾᏫ,ᏍᏙᏗ
segments.transliteration: tsi,quisdi yuwaga,da, vv elidv gali,quogi’tlv yawadetiyvda, gehv awalenvhv deganelohvsgv. sgi wawadv.sonv iga de talisgohi’tlv nawadetiyv tsigehv nahiyu tsagi,suli,gotsv oni. aginulvnv adanawi,sdodi
segments.translation: I played a lot; I started playing about seven years old. When I grew up, I quit playing about 20 years ago. I couldn’t run.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎭᏢ ᏥᏣᎴᏅᎮ ᎩᎳ ᎦᎵ,ᏉᎩ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ Ꮳ.Ꮧ?
segments.transliteration: hatlv tsitsalenvhe gila gali,quogi yudetiyvda tsa.di?
segments.translation: Where did you start playing at seven years old?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᎠᎬᏱᏛ ᎨᎲ ᏌᎷᏂ,ᎨᏴ ᎠᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᏞᏍᏗ, ᏳᎾᏙᏢᏒ ᎪᎢ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᏌᎷᏂ,ᎨᏴ ᎠᏪᏅᏒ ᎡᎵᏛᎮ ᏍᎪᎯ, ᎢᎸᏢ ᏌᏚ ᎴᏱᎦ, ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾᏃ ᎤᎾᎴᏅᎲ ᎪᎢ ᏍᎩᎾ. ᎤᏂᏧᏣ ᎠᎾᏁᏦᏍᎬ ᎦᏥᏍᏕᎵᎲ ᏂᎬ. ᏣᏁᏦᏂᏙᎲ: ᏌᎷᏂ,ᎨᏴ, ᏍᏗᎵᏪᎵ, ᏗᎦᏓᏲᏍᏗ, ᏓᏄᎪ, uh...GoreᎢ. ᎾᎿ Webber Falls. ᏧᏓᎴᏅᏓᏛ ᏬᏣᏁᏦᏂᏙᎲ.
segments.transliteration: agvyidv gehv saluni,geyv awalenvhv tlesdi, yunadotlvsv goi. sgina saluni,geyv awenvsv elidvhe sgohi, ilvtlv sadu leyiga, yawadetiyvda, nuli,stanano unalenvhv goi sgina. unitsutsa ananetsosgv gatsisdelihv nigv. tsanetsonidohv: saluni,geyv, sdiliweli, digadayosdi, danugo, uh...Gorei. nahna Webber Falls. tsudalenvdadv wotsanetsonidohv.
segments.translation: First time I started at Sallisaw; they didn’t have a field at Greasy. I went to Sallisaw. Then I was about ten or eleven years old, they started playing at Greasy. I was helping the boys play. They went all over: Sallisaw, Stilwell, Marble City, Vian, Gore, and Webber Falls. We just went everywhere to play.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎢᏥᏫᏒᏍᎬᏍ ᎨᎲ ᎢᏣᎵ,ᏍᏕᎵ,ᏙᏗ?
segments.transliteration: itsiwisvsgvs gehv itsali,sdeli,dodi?
segments.translation: Did you all plant a garden to help with food?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏂᎨᎲᎾ, ᏱᎨᎮ Ꮭ ᎠᏯ -- ᏝᏛ ᏲᏥᏂ,ᏗᏫ,ᏍᎨ ᎪᎳ. ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏗ ᎦᎵ,ᏅᏓ ,ᏚᏙ’Ꭵ ᎣᎦᏝᏫ,ᏍᏛ. ᏔᎵ, ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ,--ᏔᎵ, ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᎣᎦᏝᏫ,ᏍᏔᏂᏢ. ᎥᏍᎩ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎤᎴᏅᎲ ᎠᏫᏒᏍᎬ ᎫᏍᏗ, ᎣᏂ ᎨᏙᎲ ᎠᏯ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ. ᎤᏬᎯᏳᏒ’Ꮥ ᎠᏪᏲᎲᏍᎬ ᎠᏯ ᎨᎲ ᏕᎦᏁᎶᎲᏍᎬᏭ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎥᎩ,ᏐᎮᏗᎲ ᏕᎦᏁᎶᎲᏍᎬ. ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ, ᎠᏪᏲᏅ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎠᏫᏒᏗ. Man, ᎤᏬᏚᏛ ᏄᏩᏅ Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ, ᏴᏫ, ᎠᏂᎷᎬ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏂᏃᏎᎲ. ᎢᎦ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎤᏬᏚᏕ ᏄᏩᏅ ᏥᏳᎪ,Ꮧ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᎤᏫᏒᏅ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎣᏥᏫᏒᏍᎬ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏏᏆ ᏱᎩ, ᎣᏥᏰᎯᏍᏗ ᎣᎦᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ,. ᏍᏊᎮᎾ, ᏍᏊ ᏥᏧᏣ, ᎨᎲ ᎠᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏎ ᏥᏁᎳᏬᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎥᎾ ᎠᏩᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᏍᎩᎾ -- ᎥᎾ ᎠᏩᏕᎶᏆᏍᎬ ᎢᎸᏢ ᎠᏪᏅᏍᏗ ᏯᏩᏚᎸ ᏏᏆ, ᎣᏥᏰᎯᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ Ꮟ ᎠᏩᎵ,ᏍᏉᎵ,ᏓᏁᎮᏍᎬ ᎠᏪᏅᏍᏗ ᎠᏎᏃ, ᏁᎳᎩ, ᎠᏩᏛ.ᏐᏅ ...cause... ᎠᏮᏌ, ᎠᏩᏦᏙᏗ, ᎠᎩᎮ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎵ,ᏍᏉᎵ,ᏓᏁᎮ ᎠᏎ ᏏᏆ, ᎡᏗᎯᏍᏗ, ᏧᎾ,ᏛᏅ. ᏃᏊᎴ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏙᏣᏍᏕᎵᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎣᏥᎲ ᏏᏆ.
segments.transliteration: sgidv nigehvna, yigehe tla aya -- tladv yotsini,diwi,sge gola. udvhisdi gali,nvda ,dudo’v ogatlawi,sdv. tali, yudetiyvda,--tali, yawadetiyvda, gehv ogatlawi,stanitlv. vsgi nahiyu ulenvhv awisvsgv gusdi, oni gedohv aya sginana. uwohiyusv’de aweyohvsgv aya gehv deganelohvsgvwu sgina yudaha vgi,sohedihv deganelohvsgv. sgina tsi,quisdi, aweyonv sginana awisvdi. Man, uwodudv nuwanv tsi,quisdi, yvwi, anilugv. sgina aninosehv. iga osda uwodude nuwanv tsiyugo,di gehv na uwisvnv. sgina nigohilv otsiwisvsgv noquule siqua yigi, otsiyehisdi ogali,sdayv,di,. squuhena, squu tsitsutsa, gehv awalenvhv squu ase tsinelawosdi gehv vna awadeloquav sgina -- vna awadeloquasgv ilvtlv awenvsdi yawadulv siqua, otsiyehisdi gehv si awali,squoli,danehesgv awenvsdi aseno, nelagi, awadv.sonv ...cause... awvsa, awatsododi, agihe tla yawali,squoli,danehe ase siqua, edihisdi, tsuna,dvnv. noquule nigada, dotsasdelihv sgina otsihv siqua.
segments.translation: Yeah, if it weren’t for that. We wouldn’t have made it through the winter. An old man named Galnvd was living with us. I was two years old when he came to stay with us. That’s when he started planting a garden . I was following him around . He thought he was teaching me, but I was just playing. Sometimes they would get on to me for playing ; but he really did help me a lot about planting. He had a pretty garden, and a lot of people came and told him how pretty his garden was. Everything was all straight. We always planted a garden, and we would kill a hog for us to eat. I was young when I learned to scrape the hog. That’s when I learned I wanted to go somewhere when they going to kill a hog. They wouldn’t let me go. But even when I grew up, I had my own car, but they still wouldn’t let me go. We’re supposed to kill a hog and we would all help.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᎧᏃᎮᏍᎪ “Ꮭ ᏯᎩᎸᏉᏕ ᏬᏱ ᏱᏓᏰᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏙᏗ ᎠᏩᎾᏛ ᏏᏆ ᏛᎦᎵᏬᏥᏐᏂ.” ᏍᎩᏍ--ᏍᎩᏍ ᏗᎯᎯ ᎨᎲ ᏙᎮ?
segments.transliteration: na agi,sdayvhvsgi kanohesgo “tla yagilvquode woyi yidayesdanelv nigali,sdodi awanadv siqua dvgaliwotsisoni.” sgis--sgis dihihi gehv dohe?
segments.translation: My wife was saying she “Didn’t like when Woya was going to the house because I knew a hog was going to die.” Was he the one who killed the hog?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᏍᎩ ᎤᏍᎦᎯᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᏗᎦᏁᏩᎶ -- ᎦᏁᎳᏬᏍᏗ ᏃᏊᎴ Ꮎ ᏗᎦᏘᎯᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏝᏂᎩᏓ, ᎨᎲ. ᎡᏙᏓᎮᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᎾ,ᏓᏅᏟ, ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏬᏱ ᏚᏙ’Ꭵ.
segments.transliteration: sgi usgahidi, gehv diganewalo -- ganelawosdi noquule na digatihihv sgina utlanigida, gehv. edodahena, tsigehv dina,danvtli, gehv sgina uwoyi dudo’v.
segments.translation: He was the one that was good at scraping and sticking the hog. He was a strong man. He was my dad’s brother, his name was Uwoyi.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏂᎦᏓᏛ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᎨᏣᏚᏥ, ᏗᎨᏣᏚᏥ, ᎨᏒ ᏣᏠᎩ, ᎨᎮ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏍᏊ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᎨᎮ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: nigadadv squu sgina digetsadutsi, digetsadutsi, gesv tsatlogi, gehe nigada, squu tsalagi, aniwonisgi, gehe dohv?
segments.translation: All your uncles and aunts were Cherokee speakers, weren’t they?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎰᏩ ᏲᏁᎦ, ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ,--ᎭᏕ Ꮭ ᏯᏂᎦ,ᏔᎮ. ᏂᎪᎸ ᏱᏫ,ᎦᎯᏫ,ᏛᎯᏙᎸ ᎠᏎ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᏓ, ᎤᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᎨᎲ. ᏝᎮᎾ, ᎵᏘ, ᏚᏙ’Ꭵ ᎡᏠᎩ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏟᏴ ᎨᎲ ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎰᏩ ᏱᎪᎵ,Ꭸ ᏲᏁᎦ,. ᎭᏕ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᎩ,Ꮫ.ᎦᏅ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏲᏁᎦ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎬ. ᏃᏊᎴ ᎨᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏠᎩ, ᏍᏗ ᎠᎦ,ᏔᎲ ᏲᏁᎦ, ᏍᎩᎾᎾ. ᏃᏊᎴ ᏗᎬᎩᏚᏥ, ᎠᏧᏣ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎭᎴ ᏱᎩ, ᎠᎩ,ᏛᎦᏁ ᏍᏊ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᎲ ᎤᏔᏂᏓ, ᎠᏧᏣ. ᎾᏍᎩᎾ, ᎬᏯᏓᏂ, ᎤᏍᏗᎧᏂ, ᎤᏩᏍᎦᏢ’Ᏺ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎠᏎᏃ, Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᏱᎦᏬᏂᏍᎨ ᏲᏁᎦ, ᏱᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏁ ᎠᏎ Ꭹ.Ꮃ, ᎾᎯᏳ ᎦᏬᏂᎮ ᎠᏎᏃ, ᏍᏊ ᏙᏳ, ᏩᏍᏛ.ᏅᏭ ᏲᏁᎦ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎬ.
segments.transliteration: hesdi, howa yonega, aniwonisgi,--hade tla yaniga,tahe. nigolv yiwi,gahiwi,dvhidolv ase tsalagi, gawonida, uniwonisgi, gehv. tlahena, liti, dudo’v etlogi, tsigehv sgina utliyv gehv hesdi, howa yigoli,ge yonega,. hade tla ilvhiyu agi,dv.ganv yigehe yonega, gawonisgv. noquule gedi, tsigehv etlogi, sdi aga,tahv yonega, sginana. noquule digvgidutsi, atsutsa, tsigehv hale yigi, agi,dvgane squu tsalagi, gawonihv utanida, atsutsa. nasgina, gvyadani, usdikani, uwasgatlv’yo sginana aseno, tla howa yigawonisge yonega, yinuli,stane ase gi.la, nahiyu gawonihe aseno, squu doyu, wasdv.nvwu yonega, gawonisgv.
segments.translation: They hardly spoke English, because they didn’t know how. Every time we went to visit, you had to speak Cherokee. Lit was my aunt’s name, she didn’t really understand English. I never heard her speak English. Ged, my aunt, she knew a little English. And my uncles, Atsutsa, I never did hear his older boy speak Cherokee.* [ maybe speaker meant English] But Gvyadan, the youngest, he was hiding English. But if he had to talk, he did. But he knew very little English.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᎩ,ᏛᎦᏅ ᏱᎦᏓ ᏓᏂ-ᏓᏂ-ᏓᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᎠᏗᏔᏍᏗ ᎠᏂᏃᎮ “Mountain Dew” ᎣᏓᎸ ᎤᎯᏌᏛ. “Dr. PepperᎩ” ᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ, ᏗᏇᏲᏗ,.
segments.transliteration: agi,dvganv yigada dani-dani-daniwonisgv na aditasdi aninohe “Mountain Dew” odalv uhisadv. “Dr. Peppergi” ganaga,ti, diqueyodi,.
segments.translation: I heard him talk before, when they talk about drinking “Mountain Dew”, Odalv Uhisatv “Dr. Pepper-nv” Ganagti Digweyodi

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᎠᏧᏍᎦ’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏂᎦᏛ Ꮎ “hamburger” ᏱᎩ, ᎾᎮᎾ, ‘ᎦᏅᏩᎶᏍᏗ, Ꮵ;ᎩᎵ,’ ᏯᏓ,ᎮᎾ, ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎮᏍᏗ,ᎮᎾ, ᏲᏁᎦ, ᏱᎬᎦᏓ, ᎨᎲ.
segments.transliteration: atsusga’dv tsigehv sgina nigadv na “hamburger” yigi, nahena, ‘ganvwalosdi, tsi;gili,’ yada,hena, sginana hesdi,hena, yonega, yigvgada, gehv.
segments.translation: Tsusga (Tsigehv) he would name everything. Like, “hamburger” he called it ganvwalosdi tsigili. He wouldn’t say it in English.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏂᎯ ᏗᏣᎾ,Ꮤ ᎨᎲ ᏍᏓᏱᏍ ᏂᏓᏛᏁᎲ ᏙᎨ.?
segments.transliteration: nihi ditsana,ta gehv sdayis nidadvnehv doge.?
segments.translation: According to what you know, were we really poor, or what?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᏙᏛ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏯᎩ.ᏃᎮᏝ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾ,Ꮤ, ᎡᎵ ᏄᏛᏁᎴ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏑᏓᎵ, ᏃᏥᎲ ᏦᏥᏲᏟ,. ᎠᏮᏌ, ᏗᏇᏍᏗ, ᎤᎾᏕᏅ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎠᏩᏕᎳᎰᏒ ᎾᏍᏓᏴ ᏚᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏃᏊᎴ ᏄᏰᎵ,Ꮫ ᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏉᎵ,ᏓᏁᎸᎾ, ᎨᎲ ᏗᏩᏁᎶ,Ꮧ. ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᏥᎦᏔᎲ ᏗᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁ,Ꮧ ᏃᏊᎴ Ꭹ.Ꮆ ᎫᏍᏗ, ᏯᏬᏎᎳ, ‘ᎯᎾ ᎿᏛᎦ!’ ᏯᏬᏎᎳ, Ꮭ...I didn’t argue with them...ᏫᏂ,ᎦᏛᏁᎲ. ᎥᏍᎩᎾ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎠᏩᏕᎳᎰᏒ ᏄᏰᎵ,Ꮫ ᏍᎩ ᎾᏮᏁᎲ ᎣᏂᏃ ᎡᎵᏛ ᎠᏮᏌ, ᎠᏩᏓᏘᎾ’Ꭵ ᎠᎾᏝᏃᎮᏍᎬ Ꭹ.Ꮆ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏥᏯᏛ.ᎦᏅ. “ᎠᏂᏧᏣᏛ ᏕᎦᏛ.ᎯᏍᏔᎾ ᏍᏊ ᏅᏱ ᏱᏓᎭ ᎠᏭᏴ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᏅᏱ ᏧᏂᎲᏍᏗ ᎦᏥᏴᏁᎲ. ᏳᏂᏍᏆᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏏᏭ ᏅᏱ ᏫᏚᏂᏅ ᎤᎾ ᏙᏗᏅᏌ--Ꭳ--ᏧᏂᏗ ᏫᏕᎦᏥᏴᏁᎲ” ᎠᏗᎲ ᎠᏎᏃ, ᏙᏳ, ᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᎾᏩᏛᏁᎸ ᎠᏓ, ...but.. ᎣᏍᏓ, Ꮿ.ᏓᏅᏖᏝ ᏍᎩᎮᎾ ᏃᎬᏁᎲ ᏦᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁ,Ꮧ ᎣᎩᏁᎲ.
segments.transliteration: dodv osda, yagi.nohetla, tla yawana,ta, eli nudvnele edoda, tsigehv sudali, notsihv tsotsiyotli,. awvsa, diquesdi, unadenv nahiyu awadelahosv nasdayv dulvwi,sdanehv edoda, tsigehv. noquule nuyeli,dv nawali,squoli,danelvna, gehv diwanelo,di. gayu,la, tsigatahv digilvwi,sdane,di noquule gi.lo gusdi, yawosela, ‘hina hnadvga!’ yawosela, tla...I didn’t argue with them...wini,gadvnehv. vsgina nahiyu awadelahosv nuyeli,dv sgi nawvnehv onino elidv awvsa, awadatina’v anatlanohesgv gi.lo edoda, tsigehv. tsiyadv.ganv. “anitsutsadv degadv.histana squu nvyi yidaha awuyv, sgina nvyi tsunihvsdi gatsiyvnehv. yunisquadi sgina siwu nvyi widuninv una dodinvsa--o--tsunidi widegatsiyvnehv” adihv aseno, doyu, gehv tla sgi nawadvnelv ada, ...but.. osda, ya.danvtetla sgihena nogvnehv tsogilvwi,sdane,di oginehv.
segments.translation: If I really tell the truth, I don’t know how my dad did it, because there were six of us children. When I had my own kids, I found out how hard my dad worked. And why they wouldn’t let us play. I already knew how to work. And when somebody told me “Do this,” I didn’t argue with them, I went and did it. That’s when I realized what they were doing to me, later on, but I had my own kids. I heard somebody talking to my dad, “I raised my boys, if there were rocks laying around, I made them move them. When they moved them, I made them move them back where they got them,” he said. But he didn’t really do it, but if you really think about it —that’s what they made us do, teaching us to work.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎨᏤᏲᎲᏍᎬ.
segments.transliteration: getseyohvsgv.
segments.translation: They were teaching you.

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᎣᎨᏲᎲᏍᎬ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏯᏛᏁ,Ꮧ ᏃᏊᎴ ᎣᏥᏍᎦᏯ ᏃᎬᏁᎲ. ᎣᏂᏃ Ꮲ’ ᎡᎵᏛᎮ ᏂᎦᏚ ᏍᎩᎦᏚ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾᏃ ᏙᏳ ᎠᏂᏍᎦᏯ ᏧᏂᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁ,Ꮧ ᏙᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ. ᎾᎮᎾ, ᎤᏔᏂᏓ, ᏦᏍᏓᏓᏅᏟ, ᎤᎴᏅᎲ ᎡᎵᏛᎮ ᎦᎵ,ᏆᏚᎮ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎮ ᏧᏍᏆᏛ Ꮎ high school ᎤᎾ ᎤᎴᏅᎲ ᏚᏂᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏓᏂᏒᏢᏗᏍᎬ. ᏂᎦᏛ ᏍᎩ ᏃᎦᏛᏁᎸ high school ᏙᎩᏍᏆᏛ. ᎠᏭ,ᎮᎾ, university ᏞᎦ, ᏓᏩᏕᎶ,Ꮖ’Ꭵ ᎠᏎᏃ, ᎠᏩᏕᎳᎰᏒ ᎠᏯ Ꮎ ᎤᏍᏗᎧᏂ, ᎣᏍᏓᏓᏅᏟ, ᏗᎦᏃᏣᏟ, ᏍᏊ ᎤᏠᏱ ᏚᏍᏆᏛ ᎤᎾ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏧᎾ,ᎴᏅᎲ ᏚᏂᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏞᏍᏗ,...ᎮᏍᏗ, college ᏙᎦᏕᎶ,Ꮖ’Ꭵ.
segments.transliteration: ogeyohvsgv yusdi, yadvne,di noquule otsisgaya nogvnehv. onino tlv’ elidvhe nigadu sgigadu yawadetiyvda, nuli,stanano doyu anisgaya tsunilvwi,sdane,di dogilvwi,sdanehv. nahena, utanida, tsosdadanvtli, ulenvhv elidvhe gali,quaduhe yudetiyvda, gehe tsusquadv na high school una ulenvhv dunilvwi,sdanehv edoda, tsigehv danisvtlvdisgv. nigadv sgi nogadvnelv high school dogisquadv. awu,hena, university tlega, dawadelo,qua’v aseno, awadelahosv aya na usdikani, osdadanvtli, diganotsatli, squu utloyi dusquadv una edoda, tsuna,lenvhv dunilvwi,sdanehv sgina tlesdi,...hesdi, college dogadelo,qua’v.
segments.translation: They were teaching us what to do and they made us men. The last time when I was 14 or 15, we were really working like the men. My older brother was about 17 when he graduated high school that’s when he started working with Dad, building bridges. We all did that when we graduated. But I went to university just over here for a little while. But I realized my little brother did the same, Diganotsatli, when he graduated, he started working with my dad. We didn’t go to college .

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Ꮎ ᏐᏈᎵ, ᎠᏂᎾ,ᏌᏁᏍᎬ ᏥᎨᎲ?
segments.transliteration: na soquili, anina,sanesgv tsigehv?
segments.translation: Were they horse-drawn plows?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᎥᎥ
segments.transliteration: vv
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ, ᏓᏂ,ᏗᎮ ᎾᎯᏳ.
segments.transliteration: sgiyusdi, dani,dihe nahiyu.
segments.translation: That’s what they were using back then.

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏯᏂᎦ,ᏔᎮ tractor. Ꮭ ᏳᎾᎾ,Ꮫ tractor. ᏞᎦᎮᎾ, ᎤᎲ Dad ᏍᎩᎾ tractor. ᎠᏎᏃ, ᏂᎪᎸ ᏂᎪᎸ ᎣᏍᏗᏍᏆᏟᏍᏗᎮ ᎤᏔᏂᏓ, ᏦᏍᏓᏓᏅᏟ,. ᎤᎾᏃ ᏙᏛᏅᏓᏟ,Ꮫ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ, ᎤᏪᎵᏎ. ᏍᎩ ᎨᎲ ᏄᏪᏒ ᎣᏂ. ᎠᏬᏎ ᏙᏓᏣᏓᏟᏏᏒ ᎠᎩᏂ,ᏗᏅᏗ ᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ tractor ᎤᏛᏁ ᎠᏎᏃ, ᏙᏳ,...Ꮷ...ᎦᏅᏓ,...ᏙᎩᏳᏍᏗ, ᏴᏓ, ᎬᏩᏅ,ᏓᏗᏍᏗᏴ. -ᏓᏂ,--ᏓᏂ,ᏗᎲ ᏐᏈᎵ, ᎡᏚᏥ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎣᏍᏓᎢᏅ, ᏍᏊ ᎢᎦ ᏕᎦᎶᎨᏍᎬ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏂ-ᎠᏂ-...plow..ᎾᏅᏁᎲ.
segments.transliteration: tla yaniga,tahe tractor. tla yunana,dv tractor. tlegahena, uhv Dad sgina tractor. aseno, nigolv nigolv osdisquatlisdihe utanida, tsosdadanvtli,. unano dodvnvdatli,dv na anitsutsa, uwelise. sgi gehv nuwesv oni. awose dodatsadatlisisv agini,dinvdi nawali,sdanelv tractor udvne aseno, doyu,...tsu...ganvda,...dogiyusdi, yvda, gvwanv,dadisdiyv. -dani,--dani,dihv soquili, edutsi, tsigehv edoda, tsigehv osdainv, squu iga degalogesgv squu ani-ani-...plow..nanvnehv.
segments.translation: They didn’t know anything about tractor. Dad had one for a while, but my big brother and I, we always started the tractor. And my dad said he thought we were going to get killed. That’s why he sold the tractor —before we got killed. If I can remember, my uncle and my dad were using the horses and they really did plow a lot.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏂᎶᎩᏍᎬ
segments.transliteration: anilogisgv
segments.translation: They were hoeing the ground.

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᎠᏂᎶᎩᏍᎬ ᎥᎥ. ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎠᏂᏫᏒᏍᎬᎾ,. ᏍᎩ ᎣᏥᏧᏣ, ᏯᏛᏁ,Ꮧ ᏄᎾ, ᏕᎦᏅᏅ ᏙᏥᏢᏍᎬ ᏄᎾ,. ᏍᎩᏅ ᎠᏂᏓᎷᎩᏍᎬ. ᎥᏍᎩᎾ Ꮎ ᎦᏓ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏃᏨᏁᎲ. ᏩᎧ,--ᏩᎩᏅ ᏙᏱ, ᎤᏪᏙᎸ ᎣᏥᏢᏍᎬ ᎥᎾ ᎦᏚ. Ꮎ ‘fertilizer’ ᎣᎩᏰᎸ. ᏍᎩᏛ ᏓᏤᏢ ᎨᎲ ᏙᏳ, ᎨᎲ fertilizer ᏍᎩᎾᎾ. ᎤᎾ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ, ᎫᏍᏗ, ᏃᏣᏛᏁᎲ. ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏃᎦᏛ.ᏐᏅ. ᎤᎾ ᏭᎴᏅᎲᏃ ᎠᏮᏌ, ᏓᏄᎪ ᎣᏥᏁᎸ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏫᎩ,ᏗᎮ “Hey, ᏄᎾ, ᎡᏗᏫᏍᏗ, ᏃᏊᎴ” ᏯᏬᏎ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏊᎴ ᎦᏥᏍᏕᎴᎯᏙᎸ. ᎠᏩᏔᎾ, ᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ, Ꮟ ᏥᏍᏕᎴᎯᏙᎲ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ.
segments.transliteration: anilogisgv vv. hesdi, aniwisvsgvna,. sgi otsitsutsa, yadvne,di nuna, deganvnv dotsitlvsgv nuna,. sginv anidalugisgv. vsgina na gada, nigada, osda, notsvnehv. waka,--waginv doyi, uwedolv otsitlvsgv vna gadu. na ‘fertilizer’ ogiyelv. sgidv datsetlv gehv doyu, gehv fertilizer sginana. una sgiyusdi, gusdi, notsadvnehv. nigada, nogadv.sonv. una wulenvhvno awvsa, danugo otsinelv edoda, tsigehv nigohilv wigi,dihe “Hey, nuna, ediwisdi, noquule” yawose tsigehv noquule gatsisdelehidolv. awatana, nawali,stana, si tsisdelehidohv edoda, tsigehv.
segments.translation: Yeah, they were hoeing. Also, they were planting a garden and us boys would plant the potatoes in, and they plowed. Also we would put the dirt that the cows peed in, to put on top of the potatoes. We were using it as a fertilizer , probably was the best thing. We all grew up working like that. We were living in Vian, and my dad would call to say, “ It’s time to plant potatoes,” and I would come and help him. Even after I’ve grown up, I still help my dad.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏂᎯ ᏣᏕᎶ,Ꮖ’ᎡᏍ Ꭼ,ᏙᏗ Ꮎ ᏐᏈᎵ, ᎠᏂᎾ,ᏌᏁᏍᎬ?
segments.transliteration: nihi tsadelo,qua’es gv,dodi na soquili, anina,sanesgv?
segments.translation: Did you learn how to plow using a horse?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᎥᎥ...ᎡᎵᏛ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾ,Ꮤ, ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᎡᎵ’Ꭱ ᏂᎦᏘ,Ꮓ ᎾᏩᏝᏂᎩᏓ, ᎴᏱᎦ, ᏄᏪᎵᏌ, ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᎮᎾ, ᏧᎾᏯᏟ,Ꮧ ᏍᎩᎾ ‘ᏘᏯᏢᎩ’ ᎠᏬᏎᎲ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᏥᏍᏕᎵᎲ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ.
segments.transliteration: vv...elidv tla yawana,ta, yawadetiyvda, gehv eli’e nigati,no nawatlanigida, leyiga, nuwelisa, edoda, tsigehv nahena, tsunayatli,di sgina ‘tiyatlvgi’ awosehv. sgina sgi iga tsisdelihv sginana.
segments.translation: I don’t know how old I was, my dad used to tell me to put the bridle on to get it ready to plow. I was helping him that much.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ, ᎮᎵᏍᎨ Ꭿ-ᎯᎠ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, uh...ᏥᎩᏲᎱᏒ ᏔᎵ,ᏍᎪᎯ, ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ,ᏢᏴ? Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏕ ᎮᎵᏃ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ,?
segments.transliteration: do usdi, helisge hi-hia atsalagi, uh...tsigiyohusv tali,sgohi, yudetiyvda,tlvyv? do usde helino tsalagi, gawonihisdi,?
segments.translation: What do you think, us losing the Cherokee language? What do you think it will be like in 20 years?

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ‘Well...’ ᎾᏛ ᎤᏛ.ᎯᏍᏗ, ᏥᏥᏃᎮ. ᎦᎵ,ᏅᏓ, ᏅᏬᏘ ᏧᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ. ᎾᎯᏳ ‘ᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᎾᏂᎩᏍᎬ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᎡᏥ, ᏂᎦᏓ. ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏚᎵ ᎠᏪᏅᏍᏗ -- ᎢᎸᏢ ᏱᏩ,ᏁᎾ, ᎠᏮᏌ, ᎠᏬᏠ. Ꮎ T.V. ᏓᏩᎦ,ᏙᏍᏛ ᎥᏍᎩᎾ, ᏂᎪᎸ ᎣᏍᏓᏝᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏛ.ᎯᏍᏗ. ᎦᎵ,ᏅᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏂᎪᎸ ᏳᏪᏒ, ᎨᎲ. ᏓᎬᏃᏎᎵ,Ꮫ ᎫᏍᏗ, ᎤᏛᏅ ᎯᎾᎾ. ᏥᏗ--ᏥᏓ’Ꭲ, ᏫᏓᎩᏲᏎᎵ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᏪᏎᎮ. Ꭱ-ᎡᎵ ᏥᏧᏣ, ᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎾᏩᎾ,Ꮩ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏓᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂᏏᏒ. Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᏱᎨᎵᏍᎨ ᎠᏎᏃ, ᎥᎩ.ᏃᏎᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏛ.ᎯᏍᏗ, ᎤᎾ,Ꮫ. ᏓᏥᏲᏎᎵ,Ꮫ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ, ᏃᏭ ᏄᏪᏢᏅ. ᏃᏊᏥᎩ ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗ. ᏃᏊᎴ ᎾᏂ, ᏧᏟ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏠᏱ ᏂᎦᏪᏍᎬ. Uh...ᎤᏲ ᏓᏣᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎵ, ᏗᏥᏲᏟ,. ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏓᏥᏲᏎᎵ, ᏍᎩᎮᎾ,Ᏼ ᎤᎾᎾ,Ꮦ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎳ, ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎯᏃᎢ ᏥᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗ ᎠᏯ, ... ᎠᏯ, ᎨᎵᏍᎬ ᎨᎲ. ᏂᎦᏕ ᏗᎬ--Ꭴ....ᏙᎩ. ᎤᏍᏗ ᏴᏓ, ᏗᎬᎩ.ᏁᎸ ᎠᏎᏃ, ᏓᏥᏪᏏᏭ,. ᎮᏍᏗᎮᎾ, ᎢᎬᏌ, ᎢᏗᏣᎳᎩ, ᎢᏗᎦᏁᎳᏗ,. ᎠᏯ,ᎮᎾ, ᎤᏠᏱ ᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ, ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ, ᏗᎬᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, ᏓᎩᎧᎲ. ᎥᏍᎩᎾ, ᎠᏯ, ᎠᏮᏌ, ᏗᏪᏍᏗ, ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, Ꮭ ᏯᏂᎦ,Ꮤ. ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎤᏂᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ, ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗ ᏄᏓᎴ Ꮭ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎩᏲ Ꮝ--ᏍᎩᎮᎾ, ᎦᎵ,ᏅᏓ,ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩ ᏂᎦᏪᏍᎬ. ᎯᎾ ᏥᏓ’Ꭲ, ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ, ‘marry’ Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏴᏓ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎬᏗ,?
segments.transliteration: ‘Well...’ nadv udv.hisdi, tsitsinohe. gali,nvda, nvwoti tsulvwi,sdane gehv sginana. nahiyu ‘lvhiyu ananigisgv edoda, etsi, nigada. diniyotli, tla yawaduli awenvsdi -- ilvtlv yiwa,nena, awvsa, awotlo. na T.V. dawaga,dosdv vsgina, nigolv osdatlanohesgv sgina udv.hisdi. gali,nvda, tsigehv nigolv yuwesv, gehv. dagvnoseli,dv gusdi, udvnv hinana. tsidi--tsida’i, widagiyoseli tsalagi, awesehe. e-eli tsitsutsa, gehv nahiyu nawana,do sgina dagali,stanisisv. tla howa yigelisge aseno, vgi.nosehv sgina udv.hisdi, una,dv. datsiyoseli,dv tsalagi gawonihisdi, nowu nuwetlvnv. noquutsigi nigali,sdi. noquule nani, tsutli, tsigehv squu utloyi nigawesgv. Uh...uyo datsali,sdaneli, ditsiyotli,. tsalagi, nigada, datsiyoseli, sgihena,yv unana,te anigayvla, tsigehv. hinoi tsinigali,sdi aya, ... aya, gelisgv gehv. nigade digv--u....dogi. usdi yvda, digvgi.nelv aseno, datsiwesiwu,. hesdihena, igvsa, iditsalagi, idiganeladi,. aya,hena, utloyi nawali,stana, aniyonega, digvgi,sdayvhvsgi, dagikahv. vsgina, aya, awvsa, diwesdi, diniyotli, tla yaniga,ta. tsalagi, uniwonihisdi, nigali,sdi nudale tla tsalagi, gawonisgiyo s--sgihena, gali,nvda,hena, tsigehv sgi nigawesgv. hina tsida’i, aniyonega, ‘marry’ do usdi yvda, tsalagi, gvdi,?
segments.translation: Well the old man I was talking about, Galnvda, he made Indian medicine. They would leave him — Mom, Dad, and the children. But I didn’t want to go when they went somewhere, I would stay home and watch TV. I would always talk to the old man, Galnvda, and he would predict what was going to happen. “I’m going to tell you something,” he said, “the way we are living today, we are going to lose our language, ” he told me. I was just a little boy, and I knew that was going to happen, but I didn’t believe it. But I was told this old man knew, he said “You all are going to lose the Cherokee language.” And what he said, it is happening today. And Nan Tsutli, was saying the same thing. “You all are going to go through bad times because you all are going to lose your Cherokee language.” The old ones really knew what was going to happen. Like what is happening today, I think, people are going to get mad at me, but I’m going to say it. We didn’t marry our own kind, I did the same thing, I had white wives, so my own children don’t know how to speak Cherokee because of my wife. And Galnvda was saying, “ How we are living today, marrying white people …” How do you say marry ?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏂᏁᎳ
segments.transliteration: aninela
segments.translation: They’re married.

segments.speaker: dj-vann
segments.text: ᎥᎥ. “ᎢᏣᏁᎳ,ᏗᏍᎬ. ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ, ᏕᏥᏯᏂᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎮᎾ, ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᏓᏳᏂᏲᎱᏎᎵ, ᏣᎳᎩ,” ᎠᏗᎲ. ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏥᎦᏗ ᏃᏊᏥᎩ ᏍᎩ ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗ ᏃᏊᎴ Ꭱ--ᎠᏯ, ᎨᎲ. Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏱᏓᏩᎳᏏᏓ, ᎠᏎᏃ, ᎠᏯ, ᎤᏪᏥ ᎠᏧᏣ ᎤᏔᏂᏓ,. ᎤᎬᏫᏳ ᏚᏙ’Ꭰ, ᏥᏰᏲᎲᏍᎬ ᏣᎳᎩ, “Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏚᎵ ᎠᏩᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᏗ,” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ. ᏃᏊᎴ ᎦᏓᏅᏖᏍᎬ ᎨᎲ ᏍᏓᏱ, ᎠᏮᏂ,ᏍᏔᏂᏙᎸ ᎠᏯ,. ᏲᏁᎦ ᏥᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᏂᎨᎲᎾ ᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏚᎵᏍᎨ ᎠᏯ, ᏗᏂᏲᏟ,. ᏕᎦᏛ.ᎯᏍᏗᎲ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᏍᏓᏱ, ᎤᏂᎶᎯᏍᏗ ᏲᏁᎦ. ᎪᎯᎮᎾ ᏥᎩ ᏥᏈᏍᏗᎮᎾ ᎤᏓᏁᏟᏴᏌ, ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎩ. ᎾᎮᎾ, ‘modern’ ᏣᏂ,Ꮧ ‘i-it caught up with us. And...’ ᏍᎩᎮᎾ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎢᎦᏓ, ᏗᏂᏲᏟ,. ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᏱᎩ, ᏍᎩᎮᎾ, ᏍᏓᏱ, ᏄᎾᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁ. ᏍᏓᏱ ᏓᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂ, ᏗᎦᎵ,ᏍᏙᏗ ᎠᏯ, ᎠᏮᏌ, ᎠᎩᎶᏌ, ᏍᎩᎾ. ᏍᎩᏅ Ꭿ’Ꮎ ‘modern’ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎬᏗ,. segments.translation: Yeah, “You are marrying into white.” That’s why the children are going to lose their Cherokee language. That is what is happening today. I’m not using that as an excuse, but my oldest son, Ugvwiyu is his name, I was teaching him but, “I don’t want to learn ” he told me. I was thinking I had a hard time not speaking English growing up. I didn’t want my children to go through a hard time like I did with English. But today a lot has changed from then to now. What they call modern now, it caught up with us. That’s why kids that speak Cherokee are having a hard time. I know because I have gone through it myself. Modern, I’ll just call it “new things.” All these new things that’s coming out for the children, even the TV. I didn’t really watch TV back then. When I was a boy, we had one, but they wouldn’t let me watch it unless they were sitting there with us. When nine o’clock came we had to go to bed. They wouldn’t let us go past that time, because… If I think about it, why? Even the birds go to bed about that time. I thought, “Why did they give us that time to go to bed so early?” . When I think about it, my dad got up about 4:30 in the morning, I guess that’s why we had to go to bed early. He wanted to sleep. He didn’t want to hear the TV. I guess that’s why they made us go to bed at that time.

segments.translation: Well how I see it, it is going to be difficult for us. Because it’s coming as the older ones predicted already. Also, they say we are going to lose our language, and I believe that is going to happen. And someday the money we are using will not be of any use for us —that’s what the older ones said too. And the gardening —if you don’t know how nothing will grow (famine will happen), even if you don’t know how to hunt, or make a garden. This Walmart that we have today—when Covid-19 happened it was hard on everybody, especially those that don’t know how to cook. McDonald’s wasn’t open, cause some people that’s all they know, they don’t know how to cook. They would go get something to eat and they are the ones that it will be hardest for. They don’t know how to grow things; they just go get something. Also, like the deer— something that’s provided for us, something will happen, so we won’t be able to eat them anymore. So really, we are going to see hard times. Me, I feel sorry for my grandkids. I think about my grandma all the time. She used to scare me. I believe what she said, she was sorry for my kids. I was probably about eight years old; she was crying. I said, “What’s wrong with you? What’s going on?” “It’s going to be hard times, and your kids, and their kids are going to go through a hard time,” she said. “I don’t think I’m going to have kids because I don’t even like girls,” I told her. “You will have kids,” she said. “Cause you’re a man, you will have kids.” I still think about all that they said, my grandpa, my dad’s dad. My grandpa didn’t raise my dad. His aunt was the one that raised him. They took us to Grandpa’s house and my dad knew that they didn’t raise him. After Dad had his kids, they started talking some. That’s where we all gathered, at Grandpa’s house, and that’s what he always said, “It’s going to be difficult.” But I wasn’t listening to what the elders said. When I’m home by myself, I try to remember what they said when they spoke about the future. I wish I had listened, I’d rather have played ball with all my cousins. My grandma used to sit outside—that’s when I began to want to play baseball. I guess I was about five or six years old. I wasn’t playing yet at Sallisaw—that wood my uncle carved (uwelvsv) and the blue jeans that we are wearing today, my grandma used to cut and stuff them, then sewed them up to make balls. That’s what we had for balls. We had two and that’s what we were using playing ball, when somebody hit it too hard it tore up. And my grandma was sitting there. When it broke, she would sew it right back up. And then we started playing again. She had one of them there by her and, when, if this one broke, she would throw that other one in. I guess that’s how much she enjoyed watching us play ball. We always played ball there, and Grandma would sit on the porch watching us and laughing. That’s what I remember the most —that we played well, and because we never had fights. We never went anywhere looking for trouble while we were playing ball. I guess Grandma, she enjoyed that.

segments.translation: First, I worked at Whirlpool, where they made refrigerators, that’s where I worked. I worked about seven years there and they laid me off. Then I started working at Sallisaw, at a plant called Borg-Warner. We made water pumps for automobiles, and air filters. I probably worked there about six years. I also got laid off there. And then I started working at Vian. I was working building dams using big machinery. I’m going to say it in English, “ wastewater” … we fixed the waste water pipes. And we were always digging to put in the pipes for water to go through. And I got laid off, then I started at the Casino. I worked there 23 years, and they laid me off, I mean, I quit.
